{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABi9D3Tg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhMTQWw", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 413, "title": "Add graph-driven Floating Display for desktop and browser voice typing", "body": "## Problem

During dictation, final-only insertion can leave the user unsure whether speech is being recognized correctly while an utterance is still in progress. The user clarified that the actual need is immediate visible feedback, not insertion and later replacement of provisional text in the target document.

Both desktop and Chrome extension Web voice typing already have recording controls and the ASR nodes already expose provisional and final TEXT outputs. Add an explicit graph-controlled floating text display to both hosts rather than complicate text insertion with deletion, range tracking, or IME composition.

Current main: [d3d9f84](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/commit/d3d9f84598c79f6279a6a53e2c2b33228e18a826).
- [desktop/indicator.js](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/desktop/indicator.js) and [desktop/main.js](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/desktop/main.js): existing non-activating recording indicator.
- [extension/web-voice-content.js](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/web-voice-content.js): existing page microphone/recording control.
- [extension/web-voice-graph.js](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/web-voice-graph.js): currently selects only the focused-field sink and its ancestors, and rejects provisional edges on that path.
- #411 / PR #412 established that the generic desktop text insertion sink must honor graph wiring, not silently filter by provisional metadata.

## Expected outcome

### Shared explicit Floating Display node

Add a shared node definition (suggested type `FloatingDisplay`, label **Floating Display**) usable in desktop and Chrome extension graphs. One `text: TEXT` input, no outputs. Its sole responsibility is to show the latest supplied string in a compact floating UI during the active session. Every delivered TEXT replaces the current display snapshot; an empty string clears it. It does not accumulate, insert into the target, interpret speech IDs, select between final/provisional, or filter by producer, port name, content or provisional metadata. Any compatible TEXT producer can be wired, e.g. ASR, formatter or translation where already supported. Reuse the existing graph contracts, editor and host rendering boundaries; no new port type is required.

Recommended dictation graph:

```
MicrophoneAudio → streaming ASR
                    ├─ provisional → FloatingDisplay.text
                    └─ final       → FocusedInputTextOutputNode.text
```

A new preview replaces the previous preview visually. The producer's existing empty preview delivery clears it on completion; the sink must not infer finalization from another node or implicitly subscribe to ASR. The final output continues to be inserted by the existing output sink according to graph wiring. Show nothing extra when the floating display is unwired/absent or empty. Keep normal insertion-only graphs working. Include this branch in newly created default desktop dictation graphs and an appropriate new/example extension dictation graph or documented setup; do not silently modify existing saved user graphs. The user can add/remove the node through Graph Editor.

### Host integration and UX

- Desktop: render the supplied latest text within/adjacent to the existing non-focus-stealing recording indicator. Keep the microphone indicator and Stop affordance usable. Do not open the management window, steal input focus, or change the existing clipboard/paste and current-focus delivery behavior. Use the shared desktop UI for macOS and X11 where practical.
- Chrome extension: render the supplied latest text beside the existing on-page microphone/recording control, not inside the actual editable field. Keep it within the viewport and non-focus-stealing; use the existing isolated UI/authorized page-session transport. No new broad host permission or extra cloud processing. Enable the explicitly connected floating-display branch and its ancestors in the page-mic graph extraction, in addition to the existing field-output branch. Permit provisional connections to this display branch; do not accidentally apply the field-path-specific restrictions to it. Evaluate shared ancestors once in the same Pipeline, not a second recognition runtime. Keep unrelated Live, speaker and other side-effect branches excluded from the page-mic workflow as before. The existing field-output path behavior is not otherwise in scope.
- Make the node available in the relevant graph palettes and validators, and handle its normal runtime dispatch wherever these hosts allow execution. For extension Live/graph execution, define a coherent simple host rendering for the same node if exposed there, or explicitly document and validate a host-specific execution boundary; do not expose a node that silently does nothing. Avoid redesigning the existing Display node.
- Keep the display small and readable: latest text only, bounded width/height with sensible wrapping/overflow, no permanent explanatory paragraph, no transcript history, no new settings or mandatory confirmation. Treat displayed text as plain inert text, including HTML-like strings. Preserve accessible Stop control and existing error/status indicators. A graph without this node should retain its existing compact recording UI.
- Clear preview state on new Start and after Stop/Cancel/Quit or page-session teardown. Reject late deliveries from an ended session and isolate concurrent owners/tabs. Ordinary text updates must not block insertion or recording. Avoid excessive work on frequent updates. Prefer the simplest implementation using existing host session and display plumbing.
- Keep existing native insertion and extension field editing untouched. No provisional text replacement in third-party fields, Backspace simulation, cursor tracking, IME integration, focus-lock reintroduction, new inference model, or all-platform compatibility project. No hidden ASR-specific preview policy in generic nodes. Do not require elaborate UI placement or lifecycle race hardening beyond representative normal usage.

### Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Shared node contract and graph editor support exist on both desktop and Chrome extension. Deterministic tests show generic TEXT (including provisional and final metadata, repeated and empty updates) replaces only the floating snapshot; producer identity is irrelevant. The recommended two-branch graph displays provisional updates and inserts only final TEXT because of its wiring. Existing insertion-only graphs retain their behavior. Saved graph JSON round-trips without implicit rewiring.
- [ ] The desktop recording indicator displays successive preview strings without taking focus or changing actual target text. Existing Stop/Cancel and session authorization remain intact. The Chrome page-mic runtime executes the explicitly wired display branch alongside the insertion branch, including shared ancestors once, and renders text in the correct page session. Test ordinary update, empty clear, session end, and absence of stale previews across representative sessions. Preserve the existing unrelated branch exclusion and relevant authorization/permission boundaries.
- [ ] Provide a new/default desktop graph and an extension example or concise reproducible graph setup, plus optional manual instructions for both: start recording, observe provisional updates, confirm final text is inserted only through the final connection, and stop. Follow README UI/UX principles: Keep it simple, Show don't tell, Intuitive and predictable.
- [ ] Run `npm test`, applicable focused desktop and MV3/extension UI/runtime regression tests, affected package builds, and `git diff --check`. Use deterministic speech/worker fixtures rather than requiring real model downloads for this UI/routing change. Validate macOS as primary desktop target, preserve X11 shared behavior and run relevant checks where available. Permission-dependent native tests and human visual/manual checks remain optional; report any skipped or unavailable checks accurately. Do not delay merge for exhaustive platform/UI edge cases.

## Required post-merge verification

None. Human/manual confirmation is not a closure gate.

## Context

Follow-up to #401, #409 and #411. The user chose visual feedback instead of in-field provisional replacement. Follow the [node design principles](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/README.md#design-principles), [port contracts](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/docs/port-contracts.md), [review guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md#node-architecture) and [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md). Both hosts are required; keep the change small and share source/contracts, not running resources.
